title: Glutathione Quantification in Live Cells with Real-Time Imaging and Flow Cytometry
protocol: Seed cells 24 h before transfection at desired density in an appropriate container (2.0×10^6 cells per sample in a glass-bottom dish for imaging; 1.0×10^5 cells per well in a 12-well plate for flow cytometry).
Transfect cells with the appropriate HaloTag plasmids using Lipofectamine 3000 transfection reagent.
Culture the transfected cells for 24–48 h.
Add BSO to the cell culture medium while seeding the cells for GSH synthase inhibitor treatment.
Culture treated cells for 48–72 h in cysteine-free culture medium.
Replace cell culture medium with working solution containing RT-AM/MitoRT/HaloRT ligand.
Aspirate culture medium for adherent cells, then add the working solution.
Centrifuge non-adherent cells before removing culture medium and resuspend in working solution after addition.
Resuspend trypsin-digested adherent cells into fresh culture medium for flow cytometry experiments.
Incubate cells in the working solution for 8–10 min at 18°C–25°C for RT-AM stained cells.
Incubate cells in the working solution for 15–30 min at 37°C for MitoRT and HaloRT ligand stained cells.
Alternatively, incubate MitoRT and HaloRT ligand stained cells for 30–60 min at room temperature.
Place 10 μL of suspension containing stained cells onto a coated glass slide.
Cover the sample with a cover glass for imaging.
Seal the sample with a specific O-ring to prevent drying.
Wash cells with fresh culture medium in HaloRT ligand stained cells, and incubate cells at 37°C for 15–30 min.
Repeat washing step if signal to noise is still not optimal after one washing step.
Skip washing step for confocal imaging experiments if the signal to noise ratio is above 5.
Skip washing step for flow cytometry experiments.
Perform washing steps in flow cytometry experiments if the signal to noise ratio is below 5.
Acquire quantitative fluorescent signals using a confocal microscope or flow cytometer immediately after staining.
Use sequential imaging on two channels for confocal imaging.
Switch lines when possible, especially for smaller organelles like mitochondria.
Avoid Z-stack imaging due to its slow speed.
Maintain the same imaging conditions as those used for the calibration curve for absolute quantification.
Calculate a complex ratio (R-Rmin)/(Rmax-R) if imaging conditions are not ideal.
Advise a short imaging time for RT-AM based global GSH quantification in live cells.
Apply an appropriate non-treated, stained cell sample as control when long monitoring is needed.
Use HaloRT strategy for long-term monitoring experiments if necessary.
Increase magnification for MitoRT based mitochondria GSH (mGSH) quantification in live cells.
Consider using super-resolution imaging methods for higher resolution but with compromised quantification accuracy.
Extend imaging time for HaloRT-based organelle-specific GSH quantification in live cells.
Stain the next sample while waiting for imaging to complete, keeping staining time consistent across samples.
Create a standard curve for calibration when performing quantitative or semi-quantitative assessments.
Skip creating a standard curve for qualitative assessments if necessary.
Keep laser intensity low to prevent light toxicity and fluorophore bleaching during experiments.
Include an appropriate probe-only control for live monitoring experiments to test the clearance speed of probes in cells.
Open acquired images in Fiji ImageJ.
Duplicate each fluorescence channel into single frames.
Run background subtraction using the rolling ball algorithm with diameter 100.
Run image calculation and divide the blue channel image by the green channel image to generate a ratio map.
Change LUT (lookup table) for favorable visualization, e.g., physics.
Save all images as desired.
Mask the ratio map with regions-of-interest when necessary before quantitative analysis, especially in organelle-specific GSH measurements.
Record absolute ratio data from individual cells/organelles in all images from the dataset.
Manual picking of region of interest may be necessary.
Compare with standard curve to deduct the absolute GSH concentrations when performing quantification or semi-quantification.
In FlowJo, open the data files.
Gate by FSC and SSC to define the single-cell population.
Export the blue and green channel signal in the single-cell population to a .csv file.
Calculate the ratio in each cell by dividing signal from the blue channel by that from the green channel.
Remove outliers that are 4 standard deviations away from the mean.
Prepare two identical groups of cells by treating with increasing concentrations of BSO.
Culture one group of cells in a 12-well or 6-well plate for lysate-based assay.
Culture the other group of cells in appropriate containers as described above.
Measure GSH using standard Ellman’s assay on the group cultured for lysate-based assay.
Alternatively, measure GSH using liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry-based assay.
Analyze and record ratio value for each sample.
Compare assay results with the corresponding ratio values.
Fit the experimental data with an appropriate function based on the deviation from linearity.
Add 1 μL of 15 μm polystyrene beads suspension per 100 μL of RT solution.
Prepare a fresh GSH stock solution at 200 mM in PBS.
Adjust the pH of the GSH stock solution to 7.4 using 1.0 N NaOH solution.
Serially dilute the GSH stock solution to desired concentrations, such as 20, 10, 5, 2.5, 1.25, and 0.625 mM of GSH.
Mix an equal amount (typically 4 μL) of GSH with RT solution.
Incubate the mixture at 18°C to 25°C for 10 minutes.
Add the mixture onto a coverslip.
Cover the coverslip with a slide glass and take images.
Pipette the mixture gently to prevent beads from aggregating into one spot.
Measure Rmin using 0.01 mM of final concentration of GSH.
Measure Rmax using 100 mM final concentration of GSH.
Calculate the ratio (R−Rmin)/(Rmax−R) for each group and plot against GSH concentration to establish a linear relationship as a standard curve.
Maintain consistent conditions for calibration, including objectives, temperature, magnification, Gain/PMT, offset, filter, laser intensity settings, identical to actual imaging experiments.
Prepare single-cell suspension as described above.
Transfer 1 mL of cell suspension into a PCV tube.
Spin multiple samples for 1 min at 2,500 × g in a standard microcentrifuge.
Record pellet volume.
Count the cell number using a hemocytometer.
Calculate individual cell volume from the cell number and the total volume.
Use standard bicinchoninic (BCA) assay or other assays to measure the protein concentrations of cells.
Prepare cells the same way as the calibration group for protein concentration measurement.
Estimate cell volume using available data on the corresponding protein concentration per unit volume.
